pull.title: feat(catalogues): every field walks the ladder, and every CLI loads the file
pull.body:
# Catalogues that carry what the ladder already knows, and that every CLI will actually load

The user ran the shipped launcher and got this:

```
$ mcc-opencode models mcc
My Claude Code: 142 model(s) publish no value for one or more fields, so OpenCode falls back to its own default:
  chatgpt_oauth/gpt-5.5: limit.context, tool_call, attachment, cost
  commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash: tool_call, attachment, cost
  custom_b_ai/glm-5.3-flash: limit.context, tool_call, attachment, cost
  ... 139 more ...
Error: Configuration is invalid at C:\Users\...\.fcc\opencode-config.json
↳ Missing key provider.mcc.models.custom_b_ai/glm-5.3-flash.limit.context
↳ ... 53 more ...
```

Exit 1. Zero models listed. The 142 lines were not a warning about the failure —
they were noise in front of it.

Two causes, and the second is the interesting one.

---

## 1. The refusal: a `limit` object may not ship half-populated

`application/catalogues/opencode.py::_limit` built whichever half it knew and
`_entry` shipped it because it was truthy. Read out of the schema OpenCode
publishes (vendored at `tests/fixtures/schemas/opencode-config.schema.json`) and
reproduced against the real 1.18.26 binary:

```json
"limit": { "properties": {"context": …, "input": …, "output": …},
           "required": ["context","output"], "additionalProperties": false }
```

`limit` is **optional**; a *present* one must carry both. So the document was
rejected whole — not the entry, the document. The all-or-nothing rule was
already implemented one function down for `cost`; `_limit` simply never got it.

`_limit` now emits both keys or neither, filling an unknown half with `0` —
OpenCode's own documented unknown marker, the same value its coercion reads for
an absent `limit.context`. That keeps a known ceiling instead of discarding it
to satisfy a schema; a model with neither half known gets no `limit` at all,
which loads fine.

`cost` deliberately keeps the opposite rule and does **not** fill: a half-known
price is no price, and OpenCode publishes no spelling for an unknown *price*
the way it does for an unknown window.

## 2. The cause behind the cause: one field walked the ladder, four did not

`max_output_tokens` walked ten rungs — the routed deployment's own `/models`,
then models.dev's bucket for that provider, then the OpenRouter reference
catalogue, then a quorum-guarded cross-provider vote — and answered 124 of 128
models on this install.

`context_length`, `supports_vision`, `supports_tool_calls` and the prices
reached the same records through `enrich_model_infos`: a **flat, provider-blind,
un-tiered** name match that consults no reference bucket, strips no routing tag
and records no rung. It lands hardest on exactly the models a gateway resells.

Four siblings of `model_output_limit_tiered` now exist in
`providers/runtime/models_dev.py` — `model_context_length_tiered`,
`model_vision_tiered`, `model_tool_call_tiered`, `model_prices_tiered` — walking
the same rungs in the same order under the same minimum-sample guards, each
reporting the rung that answered.

**No rung's logic, order or quorum changed.** The diff of that file is **320
insertions and 0 deletions**:

```
$ git diff -U0 fork/main -- src/my_claude_code/providers/runtime/models_dev.py | grep '^-' | grep -v '^---' | wc -l
0
```

`capability_payload` (the Models page) and `catalogue_model._resolve` (every
generated catalogue, `/admin/api/catalogue-models`, `GET /v1beta/models`) both
consult them, with the routed deployment's own `ProviderModelInfo` winning
outright in both, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about a value or about its
provenance.

`ProviderManager.model_context_length` is deliberately **not** one of them and
stays provider-only. It feeds `application/output_tokens.py`, where an output
budget derived from a resold model's *originating* window would not fit the
deployment actually serving it. That file is unchanged.

### Page vs catalogue, measured before and after

Two GETs against the live 8082 at 2026-09-02, over the 128 normal refs present
in both payloads:

| Field | Models page (before) | Catalogue (before) | After the ladder |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context_length` | 127/128 | 128/128 | 128/128 |
| `max_output_tokens` | 124/128 | 124/128 | 124/128 |
| `supports_vision` | 125/128 | 126/128 | **127/128** |
| `supports_tool_calls` | **not on the page** | 65/128 | **125/128** |
| `input_price` / `output_price` | **not on the page** | 74/128 | **78/128** |
| `cost.cache_read` | — (no field) | — (no field) | **72/128** |
| `cost.cache_write` | — (no field) | — (no field) | **43/128** |
| `context_length` provenance tier | `null` ×128/128 | `null` ×128/128 | named per rung |

**Which investigator was right.** The tester's report measured 54 models where
the page published a context window and the catalogue said `None`, and 60 the
same for vision. The fidelity investigation measured the two as identical. On
the payload captured today they are identical to within one row — so *both were
right about the install they measured*, and neither described a code
difference: `runtime.model_context_length` reads the **enriched**
`ProviderModelInfo`, so whether it agrees with the page depends entirely on
whether `enrich_model_infos` has run against a fresh models.dev cache since the
provider catalogue was last discovered. The 54/60 gap was a stale-cache window,
not a routing difference, and it can reopen on any install after a refresh. The
ladder closes it structurally rather than by luck: **CONFIRMED**.

The gains that remain are therefore not the ones the brief predicted, and this
is the honest number: **`supports_tool_calls` 65 → 125** is the large one,
because MCC derived tool support only from `supported_parameters` and 6 of the
7 providers serving visible models on this install never publish that list.
The two cache rates go from *structurally unresolvable* to 72 and 43 of 128.

## 3. The unknown policy, re-derived from each binary

| CLI | What changed | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **OpenCode / OpenCode 2** | `limit` is all-or-nothing and fills from `0`; the two cache rates now emitted when resolved | published schema + 1.18.26 binary — CONFIRMED |
| **Kilo CLI** | its own format, with no `_mcc_defaulted` root key | 7.5.9 bundle + execution — CONFIRMED |
| **Codex** | `context_window` / `max_context_window` **omitted** when unknown, no longer `200000`; `reasoning_required` and `supports_parallel_tool_calls` removed | 0.151.0 binary — CONFIRMED |
| **Qwen Code** | comment corrected: an absent `contextWindowSize` is not "no gauge", it is `DEFAULT_TOKEN_LIMIT = 131072` | 0.15.11 bundle — CONFIRMED |
| **Pi / Crush / Command Code / Aider** | the two cache rates now resolve and are written where the CLI has a field | serialiser modules |
| everything else | policy already correct; `CLI_REQUIRED_KEYS` added so it is written down | per-module |

Codex's three deletions are all keys the binary does not read for a model:
`context_window` is `Option<i64>` with `#[serde(default)]`;
`reasoning_required` returns 0 occurrences from `grep -a -c`;
`supports_parallel_tool_calls` sits on `RawMcpServerConfig` and the MCP tool-info
struct. The last was the **single largest defaulted field in the Codex
document** — 63 of 142 models reporting substitutions into a key Codex ignores.
Codex's defaulted-model count drops **63 → 4** on the live payload.

### Kilo: two failures, one root cause

Kilo runs an excess-key check against the **root** of its config before
decoding:

```
Error: Configuration is invalid at …\kilo\kilo.json
↳ Unrecognized key: _mcc_defaulted
```

Through `KILO_CONFIG` it is worse, not better: that load path wraps the parse in
`catchDefect` and swallows the failure into an empty object, so the provider
simply vanishes — `kilo models` lists 300 built-ins, none of them MCC's, exit 0,
no error. That is what a user actually saw, and it is why `KILO_CONFIG` looked
broken. It is not: it works, and the marker key was the whole problem.

## 4. Catalogue contents

* **`:batch` refs leave the pickers.** An asynchronous pricing tier is not a
  second interactive model. They stay in `/v1/models`. **142 entries → 82.**
  `.env.example` carries a commented `MODEL_VISIBILITY_DENY=*:batch` for hiding
  them everywhere.
* **A surviving `claude-3-freecc-no-thinking/` twin is re-projected onto its
  plain ref** and states `reasoning: false` in the CLI's own words. Such a twin
  only exists where the provider reported the model cannot think, so that is a
  statement rather than a guess. Nothing routes differently: the plain gateway
  id is the normal routing id, and the prefix is a Claude Code client-side
  heuristic with no other consumer (`grep` for `no_thinking_gateway_model_id`
  returns `api/model_catalog.py` and the id builder only).
* **`GET /v1beta/models` goes through the same collapse.**
  `api/gemini_model_catalog.py` enumerated the raw records, so it published both
  the normal record and the twin for every ref while every generated catalogue
  published one. Undocumented asymmetry, now closed.
* **Visibility already filtered the catalogue** and nothing asserted it. It does
  now.

## 5. The tester's remaining findings

* **Cline, Crush and Goose** seeded on the first catalogue entry, which on this
  install was a free tier the provider had withdrawn — every session opened on a
  model that 404s. They now start on the route named by `MODEL`, else the first
  non-free entry, and say which.
* **Aider mutated the cwd**, appending `.aider*` to the working tree's
  `.gitignore` and `git init`ing a directory that is not a repository. Launched
  with `--no-gitignore` now; `--gitignore` after it still wins.
* **Gemini CLI needs `--skip-trust` headless.** Documented as an invocation, not
  set: workspace trust is the user's decision, not the proxy's.

## 6. The 142-line stderr wall

One line, with the field histogram:

```
My Claude Code: 39 model(s) carry a value OpenCode supplied because no provider
published one (cost.cache_write x35, cost.cache_read x6, cost x4, limit.output x4,
reasoning x3, tool_call x3, attachment x1). Details: the Coding agents page, or
set MCC_CATALOGUE_VERBOSE=1.
```

Real output, produced by resolving the captured live records through the new
lookups and running the real serialiser. Compare the shipped line: **142
model(s)**, followed by 142 more.

The per-model detail moves behind `MCC_CATALOGUE_VERBOSE=1`. It has two other
homes — the generated file's own `_mcc_defaulted` block and the Coding agents
card — so stderr is a pointer rather than a third copy. The summary is read from
`/admin/api/catalogue-models` rather than from the written document, which is
also how Kilo still reports its counts.

### Defaulted-field census, before and after

Live capture serialised through both builds. "Before" is the document the
running server produced today; "after" is the same records resolved through the
new lookups and run through the new serialisers.

| Harness | models before → after | models with ≥1 CLI default, before → after |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode` / `opencode2` / `kilo` | 142 → **82** | 142 → **39** |
| `codex` | 142 → **82** | 69 → **3** |
| `pi` | 142 → **82** | 142 → **39** |
| `commandcode_cli` | 142 → **82** | 142 → **39** |
| `crush` | 142 → **82** | 142 → **39** |
| `aider` | 142 → **82** | 133 → **39** |
| `qwen_code` | 142 → **82** | 68 → **3** |
| `kimi_code` | 142 → **82** | 62 → **3** |
| `droid` | 142 → **82** | 63 → **4** |
| `gemini_cli` | 142 → **82** | 10 → **4** |
| `cline_cli` | 1 → 1 | 56 → **4** |

`limit.context` — the key that refused the launch — goes from **54** to **0**.
The residual `cost.cache_write ×35` is genuine: models.dev publishes a cache
write rate for 43 of the 128 refs and nothing else does.

## 7. The test that was missing

`tests/contracts/test_catalogue_schema_contract.py`: **real payload → real
serialiser → real schema.**

It loads `tests/fixtures/catalogue_models_live_shaped.json` — a 270-record
capture of the live `/admin/api/catalogue-models` `models` array, 7 providers,
126 rows with no `supported_parameters` at all, no credentials and no URLs —
serialises it through every format, and validates the result against each CLI's
own published schema, vendored so the suite never needs the network.

Verified to catch the original defect. With `_limit` restored to its old
behaviour over that fixture:

```
REJECTED as expected: 'output' is a required property
```

Six harness PRs shipped before this because every fixture was one or two models
with hand-set capabilities, and the nearest existing test asserted no
limit-shaped key was `0` — for OpenCode the key was *absent*, so it passed
vacuously while guarding a document OpenCode refused.

Every serialiser now declares `CLI_REQUIRED_KEYS` beside its
`CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS`, recovered from a shipped binary or a published
schema, and a test holds every format to it.

---

## Real-CLI validation matrix

Both documents were generated from the **same** captured live payload — the
shipped serialisers for "before", this branch's for "after" — and handed to the
**real binaries** in a scratch `HOME` (`HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `APPDATA`,
`LOCALAPPDATA`, `XDG_{CONFIG,DATA,STATE,CACHE}_HOME`, `CODEX_HOME` all
redirected). No server was started and **no request was sent to 127.0.0.1:8082**
— the change is to what a CLI is handed, so config load and validation is the
load-bearing evidence. A post-run audit of every real config path shows zero
files modified.

| Harness (command) | before exit | before first error | before `mcc/` | after exit | after first error | after `mcc/` | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`opencode`** `OPENCODE_CONFIG=... opencode models` | **1** | `Configuration is invalid ...` | **0** | **0** | *(none)* | **82** | CONFIRMED |
| `opencode2` `... opencode2 models` | 0 | *(none — provider silently dropped)* | **0** | 0 | *(none)* | **82** | CONFIRMED |
| `kilo` (a) `KILO_CONFIG=... kilo models` | 0 | *(none — swallowed)* | **0** | 0 | *(none)* | **82** | CONFIRMED |
| `kilo` (b) `KILO_CONFIG=... kilo config check` | **1** | `Unrecognized key: _mcc_defaulted` | n/a | 0 | `No config warnings.` | n/a | CONFIRMED |
| `kilo` (c) file at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/kilo/kilo.json` | **1** | `↳ Unrecognized key: _mcc_defaulted` | **0** | 0 | *(none)* | **82** | CONFIRMED |
| `codex` `codex -c model_catalog_json=... debug models` | 0 | *(none)* | 142 slugs | 0 | *(none)* | 82 slugs | CONFIRMED |
| `crush` `crush -D <scratch> models` | 0 | *(none)* | 142 | 0 | *(none)* | 82 | CONFIRMED |
| `aider` `--no-gitignore --model-metadata-file ... --list-models` | 0 | *(none)* | 128 | 0 | *(none)* | 82 | CONFIRMED |
| `droid` `droid doctor` | 0 | `[ok] Configuration files` | 142 | 0 | `[ok] Configuration files` | 82 | CONFIRMED |
| `kimi` `kimi --config-file ... --print -p hi` | 1 | *(generator artefact, see below)* | 0 | 1 (runtime `LLM not set`) | config parsed | **82** | CONFIRMED |
| `gemini` `GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH=... gemini mcp list` | 0 | *(none)* | n/a | 0 | *(none)* | n/a | CONFIRMED |
| `cline` `cline doctor` | 0 | *(none)* | n/a | 0 | *(none)* | n/a | **UNVERIFIED** |
| `qwen_code` `qwen mcp list` | 0 | *(none)* | n/a | 0 | *(none)* | n/a | **UNVERIFIED** |
| `commandcode_cli` `command-code --list-models` | 0 | *(none)* | 142 | — | — | — | before only |
| `goose` | n/a | env-only, no document | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |

### The headline row, verbatim

**before** — exit 1, stdout empty, stderr complete:

```
Error: Configuration is invalid at .../before/docs/opencode-config.json
> Missing key provider.mcc.models.opencode/claude-fable-5-1.limit.output
> Missing key provider.mcc.models.nous_portal/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:US.limit.output
> Missing key provider.mcc.models.commandcode/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-fast.limit.output
> Missing key provider.mcc.models.custom_b_ai/gpt-5.5-instant.limit.output
```

**after** — exit 0, stderr empty, 590 rows of which 82 begin `mcc/`:

```
mcc/opencode/big-pickle
mcc/opencode/mimo-v2.5-free
mcc/anthropic/claude-fable-5-1
mcc/nous_portal/meituan/longcat-2.0:free
...
```

**One correction to my own framing.** The user's original failure was 52 x
`limit.context` + 2 x `limit.output`. Reproduced against the payload captured
*today*, it is 4 x `limit.output` — because the 54 context gaps had since been
filled by an `enrich_model_infos` pass against a refreshed models.dev cache.
Same bug, same rejection, fewer entries triggering it on this particular day.
It is still fatal: four half-populated objects refuse the whole document and
list zero models, exactly as fifty-four did.

### Each validating command was itself validated

A command that exits 0 on a broken config proves nothing, so every row was
controlled with a deliberately corrupt document:

| CLI | corrupt-config control | result |
|---|---|---|
| codex | `slug` removed | exit 1 — ``missing field `slug` `` |
| crush | truncated | exit 1 — `Failed to load config from paths` |
| gemini | truncated | exit 52 — `Unexpected end of JSON input` |
| droid | truncated | exit 1 — `line 2, col 1: ValueExpected` |
| kimi | broken TOML | exit 1 — `Invalid TOML in configuration file` |
| **cline** | truncated | **exit 0** — `doctor` ignores it |
| **qwen** | truncated | **exit 0** — no non-interactive validating path in 0.15.11 |

The last two are why those rows read UNVERIFIED rather than PASS. `cline config`
requires a TTY and `qwen --list-extensions` fails on auth before it reaches
settings; neither document produced a parse error, but that is a weak pass and
is reported as one.

### Codex, specifically

`codex debug models` loads the after-catalogue with **exit 0 and 82 models, no
`missing field`**. `supports_parallel_tool_calls` goes 205 occurrences -> 0 and
`reasoning_required` 21 -> 0. `context_window` is still present on all 82,
because on this payload every model has one — the change is that an *unknown*
window is now omitted rather than written as `200000`, which the unit tests
cover directly.

### Not reproduced, and why

* **`commandcode_cli` after**: MCC delivers that catalogue by *merging* into the
  user's own `~/.commandcode/providers.json`, and the offline generator used
  here writes only stand-alone documents. The before side was exercised (exit 0,
  205 models of which 142 `mcc`); there is no after counterpart to compare
  against and a synthetic merge was not forced.
* **`pi`**: `process_local` delivery — no file exists to validate.
* **`kimi` before**: reported a TOML parse error, but that is an artefact of the
  offline before-generator dumping the payload's document as JSON. The shipped
  server writes it through `config/harness_toml.py`. **Not a product defect and
  not claimed as one**; the after side is real TOML and loads with 82 models.
* **`opencode2`**: the first four after-runs timed out on a background service
  left running by the before-run. After killing it, both phases reproduced twice.

---

## Screenshots

`screenshots-fidelity/coding-agents-kilo-card.png` — the Coding agents page on a
scratch server (port 8199, scratch `HOME`, never the live 8082) showing OpenCode
reporting its defaulted count from the file and Kilo CLI reporting instead that
its schema will not hold the record. Zero console errors.

## Tests

* New: `tests/contracts/test_catalogue_schema_contract.py` (52 cases),
  `tests/providers/test_models_dev_field_ladder.py` (6),
  `tests/fixtures/live_catalogue.py` + the 270-record fixture, plus new cases in
  `test_admin_models_page.py` (4), `test_opencode_serialiser.py` (3),
  `test_catalogue_model.py` (2), `test_serialiser_contract.py` (3),
  `test_opencode_launcher.py` (3), `test_gemini_api.py` (1),
  `test_admin_static_jsdom.py` (1).
* Changed deliberately: the nine tests that pinned the
  `claude-3-freecc-no-thinking/` prefix on a surviving twin, Codex's three
  removed keys, and
  `test_optional_unknown_fields_are_omitted_not_zeroed` — narrowed to the keys
  that are genuinely optional on their own, because blurring "optional key" and
  "optional object with required members" is how the defect passed review.
* jsdom: `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py -n 0` → **196 passed** (195
  before, +1 new).
* `uv run --offline ruff format --check .` → 1126 files already formatted;
  `ruff check` and `ty check` clean over `src/`, `tests/` and `scripts/`.

**Local baseline note.** The full suite reports 15 pre-existing local failures
plus jsdom errors under full parallel load. Rerun with a clean `HOME`
(`tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_…` and the
seven `tests/websearch` / `test_web_server_tools` cases) they all pass — they
read the developer's real `~/.fcc/anthropic_oauth.json` and `EXA_API_KEY`. The
PowerShell installer cases and the jsdom errors are the documented flakes; jsdom
run alone is green at 196.

## Residual risks

1. **The cross-provider vote now decides more fields.** `tool_call` and the
   cache rates can be answered at tiers 7-10 — a modal value across rows that
   merely share a name. The same three-reporter quorum applies and the rung is
   reported and badged `approximate`, but a wrong `tool_call: true` for a model
   that cannot call tools would surface as a tool-use failure rather than as an
   absent capability. **Accepted:** the alternative is what shipped, which was
   63 of 142 models defaulting to `tool_call: true` anyway, unrecorded.
2. **Price tie-breaks resolve toward the lower number**, unlike limits and
   booleans which resolve toward the more capable reading. That is a judgement
   call written down in `_LadderField`, not a measurement.
3. **Codex's `availability_nux` and `upgrade`** appear in the binary's
   `ModelInfo` field list without an obvious `#[serde(default)]`. MCC does not
   emit them and Codex loads the catalogue anyway, so they are treated as not
   required — **UNVERIFIED** by direct probe.
4. **Six serialisers' unknown policies still rest on their own docstrings.**
   Crush and Cline were confirmed against binaries this round; Pi and Droid were
   not, and Command Code's `--list-models` shortfall (116 of 142) reported by
   the tester remains unexplained.
5. **`GET /v1beta/models` now lists fewer models than `/v1/models`.** That is
   the intended shape — a picker versus a protocol surface — but it is a
   user-visible change to a published route and is documented in ARCHITECTURE
   and USAGE rather than versioned as breaking, because no id changed meaning.
6. **The live 8082 was not restarted**, so none of this is running there yet.
   Everything measured against it is the *old* build's output used as input.
7. **A re-projected no-thinking twin loses its server-side reasoning
   suppression.** The `claude-3-freecc-no-thinking/` id decodes to
   `force_reasoning_off=True` in `application/routing.py`; the plain id takes
   the configured `reasoning_policy` instead. For the models this affects that
   is inert — they are re-projected *because* their provider reported they
   cannot think, and the record states `can_reason=False` — but it stops being
   inert if a provider's `supports_thinking` is wrong. On this install all 14
   such refs are `:batch` and are excluded anyway, so the path is dormant here:
   **CONFIRMED dormant, UNVERIFIED against a non-batch example.**
8. **`cline` and `qwen` config loading is UNVERIFIED.** Neither CLI has a
   non-interactive command that provably validates the document MCC writes —
   both exit 0 on a deliberately corrupt one, so their rows in the matrix are
   reported as weak passes rather than passes.

commit.message:
feat(catalogues): every field walks the ladder, and every CLI loads the file

`mcc-opencode models mcc` printed 142 lines saying which numbers nobody
published, then refused to start: 52 entries carried a `limit` object with
`output` and no `context`, 2 the reverse, and OpenCode answers a partial
`limit` by rejecting the whole document rather than the entry. Zero models
listed. The 142 lines were not a warning about the failure; they were noise in
front of it.

Two causes, and the second is the interesting one.

`application/catalogues/opencode.py::_limit` built whichever half it knew and
`_entry` shipped it because it was truthy. Read out of the published schema and
reproduced against the real binary, `limit` is an optional object with
*required members*: present means `context` and `output` together. The
all-or-nothing rule was already implemented one function down for `cost` and
`_limit` simply never got it. `limit` now emits both keys, filling an unknown
half with `0` -- OpenCode's own documented unknown marker -- so a known ceiling
survives instead of being discarded to satisfy a schema, and a model with
neither half known gets no `limit` at all.

The second cause is why the default was reached 54 times. `max_output_tokens`
walked a ten-rung ladder -- the deployment's own `/models`, then models.dev's
bucket for that provider, then the OpenRouter reference catalogue, then a
quorum-guarded cross-provider vote -- and answered 124 of 128 models.
`context_length`, `supports_vision`, `supports_tool_calls` and the prices
reached the same records through `enrich_model_infos`: a flat, provider-blind,
un-tiered name match that consults no reference bucket, strips no routing tag
and records no rung. That is the whole asymmetry, and it lands hardest on
exactly the models a gateway resells.

`model_context_length_tiered`, `model_vision_tiered`, `model_tool_call_tiered`
and `model_prices_tiered` are siblings of `model_output_limit_tiered` in
`providers/runtime/models_dev.py`: the same rungs, the same order, the same
minimum-sample guards, each reporting the rung that answered. The existing walk
is untouched -- the diff of that file is 320 insertions and no deletions.
Measured against the live catalogue and the live models.dev cache, over the 128
normal refs: `supports_tool_calls` 65 -> 125, `cache_read` 0 -> 72,
`cache_write` 0 -> 43, prices 74 -> 78, vision 126 -> 127, context already 128.

`capability_payload` and `catalogue_model._resolve` both consult them, with the
routed deployment's own record winning outright in both, so the Models page and
a generated file cannot disagree about a value or about its provenance. The
Models page now shows a tier for every resolved field, not only the output
ceiling, and carries `supports_tool_calls` and all four price rates for the
first time. `ProviderManager.model_context_length` is deliberately not one of
them and stays provider-only: an output budget derived from a resold model's
originating window would not fit the deployment serving it, and
`application/output_tokens.py` is unchanged.

Then the unknown policy per CLI, re-derived from each binary rather than from
this repo's own docstrings:

* Codex 0.151.0 does **not** require `context_window` -- it is
  `Option<i64>` with `#[serde(default)]` -- so writing `200000` for an unknown
  window was the exact literal this module was created to remove, reinstated
  one field over. Omitted and recorded now. `reasoning_required` does not occur
  in the binary at all and `supports_parallel_tool_calls` lives on
  `RawMcpServerConfig`, not `ModelInfo`; both are gone, taking the largest
  defaulted field in the Codex document with them (63 of 142 models).
  Defaulted models: 63 -> 4 on the live payload.
* Kilo CLI 7.5.9 runs an excess-key check against the root of its config and
  throws `Unrecognized key: _mcc_defaulted`. Through `KILO_CONFIG` it is worse:
  that load path swallows the failure, so the provider vanishes with no error
  and `kilo models` lists 300 built-ins and nothing of MCC's -- which is what a
  user actually saw. Kilo gets a format of its own that omits the root record;
  its counts reach the launcher and the card from the catalogue route instead,
  and the card says so rather than reporting a zero nobody measured.
* Qwen's comment claimed an absent `contextWindowSize` leaves it without a
  gauge. It does not: `tokenLimit` falls back to `DEFAULT_TOKEN_LIMIT =
  131072`. The policy was right and the reasoning was wrong, which is the kind
  of claim the next serialiser gets modelled on.

`:batch` refs leave the pickers -- an asynchronous pricing tier is not a second
interactive model -- and stay in `/v1/models`. A `claude-3-freecc-no-thinking/`
twin that survives the collapse is re-projected onto its plain ref and states
`reasoning: false` in the CLI's own words, because that prefix is a Claude Code
heuristic and the twin only exists where the provider said the model cannot
think. 142 entries become 82. `GET /v1beta/models` goes through the same
collapse, closing an asymmetry where it published both records per ref while
every generated catalogue published one.

Cline, Crush and Goose have to name one model to open a session. They took the
first entry, which on this install was a free tier the provider had withdrawn,
so every session opened on a model that answered 404. They now start on the
route named by `MODEL`, or the first non-free entry when that is hidden, and
say which.

The 142-line stderr wall becomes one line with a field histogram; the per-model
list moves behind `MCC_CATALOGUE_VERBOSE=1` and still has two other homes.
Aider is launched with `--no-gitignore`, because launching a coding agent must
not `git init` the user's directory or edit their `.gitignore`.

Finally the test that was missing: `tests/contracts/test_catalogue_schema_contract.py`
serialises a 270-record capture of the live catalogue -- 7 providers, 126 rows
with no `supported_parameters` at all -- and validates the result against each
CLI's own published schema, vendored under `tests/fixtures/schemas/`. Verified
to fail on the original defect: with `_limit` restored to its old behaviour the
document is rejected with `'output' is a required property`. Every serialiser
now declares `CLI_REQUIRED_KEYS` beside its `CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS`, so what
